Dayi left-side paging panel for physical keyboards

Designed for external physical keyboards: the \"▲ (page up) / ▼ (page down)\" paging controls are moved to the far left, so you can type with your right hand and page with your left. The buttons light up according to the available pages, greatly reducing hand movement fatigue and mistaps.

Drops the traditional XML title bar so the settings screen extends to the top edge, combined with a minimal left navigation bar and a frosted-glass gradient background, freeing up more than 15% of reading space for a refined look.
The Dayi smart selection module is upgraded to an \"AI smart core\" with a new breathing status light. When enabled it glows green and softly lights the whole card to show the engine state.
If the input method misbehaves or mapping tables are missing, tap \"Reset settings\" at the bottom of the left navigation panel to restore the factory settings. This solves more than 95% of problems.
After installing new mapping tables, make sure the \"Enable Dayi\" and \"Enable Chuyin\" switches are on.
While typing, use your right hand on the physical keyboard to enter key codes and candidate number keys.
To page, tap \"▲ (previous page)\" and \"▼ (next page)\" at the far left edge of the tablet screen with your left hand.
Physical keyboards can commit words directly by default. You can also turn on \"Sort by selection on physical keyboard\" in Settings to keep frequently used words at the front.
Dayi left-side paging for external physical keyboards (▲/▼).
Upgraded the two-pane full-screen immersive settings console on tablets and hid the XML AppBarLayout.
Redesigned the Dayi smart selection AI card and added a green/grey breathing status light.
Moved Help and Reset to the bottom of the navigation bar.
Simplified the architecture by removing the old voice input key and VoiceInputActivity.
Added 66 passing unit test cases for LimeDB, IMSwitchHelper and OptionsDialogHelper.
Fixed the emoji keyboard (Emoji Picker) interrupting input and crashing the input method when switched to.
Improved input method startup stability and system integration.
Adopted Material Design 3 throughout, with dynamic color and edge-to-edge display.
Fixed random crashes caused by the side menu.
Changed the version format to a date (yyyy.MM.dd) for easier identification.
